bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar sets up committee to review assistant professor recruitment system , suggest reforms
bihar_raw_news.content: India's Best Colleges 2026 Home News Bihar sets up committee to review assistant professor recruitment system, suggest reforms ADVERTISEMENT Bihar sets up committee to review assistant professor recruitment system, suggest reforms The committee includes retired IAS officers Amarjit Sinha and Sanjay Kumar, physicist and Padma Shri awardee Professor H.C. Verma, along with two other members. Curated by Mansi Image: File photo Sep 14, 2026 Share The Bihar government has set up a high-level committee to examine the existing process for recruiting assistant professors in state universities and suggest changes to the system. The move follows weeks of protests by PhD holders and researchers who have sought changes in the recruitment process, including a higher upper age limit and objective-type written examinations. According to PTI, the committee will review various aspects of assistant professor recruitment and recommend reforms to the current system. Panel to review assistant professor recruitment process The committee includes retired IAS officers Amarjit Sinha and Sanjay Kumar, physicist and Padma Shri awardee Professor H.C. Verma, along with two other members. Sanjay Kumar, additional secretary (university) in the Governor's Secretariat, will serve as the member secretary of the committee. Dipak Kumar Singh, additional chief secretary to the Governor, announced the formation of the panel on Saturday. The committee will examine several parts of the existing recruitment process. These include the upper age limit, eligibility criteria, examination and interview formats, and the weightage given to different selection parameters. The panel will also consider matters related to guest lecturers and other issues connected with the recruitment system before proposing changes. Committee formed after agreement with researchers' association The committee was formed following an agreement reached on August 24 between Bihar Governor Lt Gen (Retd) Ata Hasnain and representatives of the All PhD Holders and Researchers Association, according to PTI. The association had demanded changes to the assistant professor recruitment system and held a three-week protest in Patna last month. The demonstrations took place at Gardani Bagh, the designated protest venue in the state capital. Some participants also went on hunger strikes during the protest. PhD holders demand higher age limit, objective tests One of the association's main demands was to raise the maximum age limit for appointment as an assistant professor to 55 years. The protesters also called for objective-type written examinations as part of the recruitment process. The agitation ended after representatives of the association held a two-hour meeting with Governor Hasnain. During the meeting, the Governor assured the delegation that a committee of educationists and administrators would be formed within 15 days to consider their demands, PTI reported. Panel to examine wider recruitment reforms The committee's work will cover more than the specific demands raised by the protesters. It will assess the wider structure of assistant professor recruitment and recommend changes based on its findings. The review could cover eligibility requirements, examination and interview formats, and other criteria used to select assistant professors in Bihar's state universities. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar becomes first state in India to launch dedicated investment policy for sugar industry
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News AI Representational Image Patna: In what is being described as a first-of-its-kind initiative in the country, the Bihar government has announced a direct grant of Rs 14 crore per year for five consecutive years to investors who set up new sugar mills in the state, taking the total payout to Rs 70 crore per mill over five years. The move is part of the newly launched Bihar Sugarcane Industry Investment Promotion Policy-2026, which came into force just a few days ago, The Times of India reported. State Sugarcane Commissioner Anil Kumar Jha confirmed to media that the grant will be disbursed in equal annual instalments of Rs 14 crore, with the first instalment released just one month after the new mill begins operations. To be eligible, a new sugar mill must have a minimum crushing capacity of 3,500 tonnes per day. Investors looking to go beyond the base capacity will find additional incentives waiting. For every extra 100 tonnes of crushing capacity added above the 3,500 tonne threshold, the government will provide an additional Rs 2 crore, making larger investments progressively more attractive. The policy also addresses one of the most significant challenges for new industrial projects – land. The government has linked land support directly to the size of the plant. An investor setting up a mill with a capacity of 5,000 tonnes per day will be eligible for up to 40 acres of land on lease at a token payment of just Re 1. For a mill at the minimum capacity of 3,500 tonnes per day, up to 25 acres will be made available on the same terms. On top of this, the policy provides full reimbursement of registration fees and stamp duty on land purchased for setting up new sugar mills. The policy does not stop at new investments. Existing and operational sugar mills looking to expand their capacity will also benefit. The government will provide Rs 15 crore for a capacity expansion of 1,000 tonnes per day, with an additional Rs 1.5 crore offered for every further 100 tonnes of expansion beyond that. What sets this policy apart from those of other states, according to Jha, is that Bihar has created a standalone investment promotion framework exclusively for the sugarcane industry. Every other state in the country, he said, folds sugarcane-related incentives into broader industrial policies. Bihar’s decision to carve out a separate policy for this sector is being seen as a strong signal of the state government’s intent to revive and grow its sugar industry. Jha also said that the incentives and land support on offer in Bihar are more generous than what any other state currently provides. The government has set an ambitious target behind this policy – to establish 25 new sugar mills across Bihar and restart nine mills that have been shut down, all within the next five years. The policy is also expected to generate employment for one crore youth in the state

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed gratitude to the leaders of all the BRICS member countries for making the Delhi summit of the grouping productive and outcome-oriented. A video reflecting key moments of the two-day summit was posted on the social media handles of the prime minister. In the video, a part of the prime minister’s summit speech was shown where he said through BRICS, India has advanced friendship, partnership and cooperation all across. The leaders who attended the summit included Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi’s Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, President of the Philippines Ferdinand R Marcos Jr, Uganda’s Vice President Jessica Alupo, besides others, also attended the summit. India hosted the BRICS Summit on September 12-13 and it was attended by the leaders of the 11 member countries and 10 partner countries of the grouping, besides some international organisations. Mr Modi also held 15 sit-down bilateral meetings with heads of states or heads of governments in the last three days on the sidelines of the summit.

national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 24 HM Amit Shah says, BJP-led NDA governments in 21 states will introduce Uniform Civil Code before ...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that BJP-led NDA governments in 21 states will introduce Uniform Civil Code (UCC) before 2029. Speaking to reporters in Mumbai, Home Minister said, UCC has been introduced in several states and he is confident that it will be introduced in the 21 BJP-NDA ruled states before 2029. Mr Shah said, triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. He said the government has strengthened the country’s criminal justice system through the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and claimed that several states have recorded a 30 per cent increase in the conviction rate in a single year. Home Minister also said a system is being established to ensure justice ccan be delivered within three years. On national security, Mr Shah said the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A had been achieved without a single drop of blood being shed or a bullet being fired, and asserted that Kashmir is now fully integrated with India. He said the government has ended five decades of Naxalism and signed more than 14 peace agreements in the country’s North-East region. Mr Shah said, surgical strikes, air strikes and Operation Sindoor have established a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism.

national_raw_news.title: 53 mins ago | National 46 Hindi Diwas celebrated across the country today
national_raw_news.content: Hindi Diwas is being celebrated across the country today. It was on this day in 1949 that the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi written in Devanagari script as the official language of the country. Today, Hindi is one of the widely spoken languages in the world and the first language of more than 52 crore people. Union Home Minister Amit Shah will attend the Hindi Diwas 2026 program and the 6th All India Rajbhasha Sammelan (Official Language Conference) in Navi Mumbai today. The two-day All India Official Language Conference is being organised in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, by the Department of Official Language under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The conference aims to highlight the relationship between Hindi and Maharashtra’s rich linguistic, cultural and literary traditions. In the inaugural session today, Union Home Minister Amit Shah will present the ‘Rajbhasha Gaurav’ and ‘Rajbhasha Kirti’ Awards for 2025-26. Several important books and publications will also be launched. An exhibition featuring stalls by various institutions, organisations, banks and ministries is also being organised. A key attraction of this year’s conference will be a discussion centred on the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, several Members of Parliament, scholars, litterateurs, educationists and senior officials will attend the conference.

national_raw_news.title: 59 mins ago | Sports 41 India wins record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, President Murmu congratulates team
national_raw_news.content: India produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai last night, securing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. The victory also helped India avenge their defeat to Sri Lanka in the 2024 final. It was India’s sixth win over Sri Lanka in an Asia Cup final across the ODI and T20 formats, including the 2004 edition when India defeated Sri Lanka 5-0 in the two-team tournament. India first posted a formidable 183 for 5 after openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking 129-run partnership. The bowlers then completed the job by dismissing Sri Lanka for 111 in 19.4 overs, with Shree Charani taking four wickets and Deepti Sharma claiming three. Shafali Verma was declared Player of the Match. India’s victory was built on a combination of explosive batting at the top and disciplined bowling through the middle and final overs. The record partnership between Shafali and Mandhana gave India the platform, while Charani and Deepti dismantled Sri Lanka’s chase to seal a memorable eighth title. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. In a social media post, the President said that the players played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches and making the country proud. She said that these players are a source of great inspiration for the youth of the country. She also expressed confidence that the team will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence.

national_raw_news.title: PIB Press Tour offers Arunachal journos a glance into innovation, infrastructure & cultural heritage
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News PIB Press Tour offers Arunachal journos a glance into innovation, infrastructure & cultural heritage | Tapan Kr DAS | ITANAGAR, Sep 13: A Press Information Bureau (PIB), Itanagar-sponsored press tour to Gujarat provided a nine-member media delegation from Arunachal Pradesh with an opportunity to explore a diverse range of development initiatives, institutions, technological innovations and cultural landmarks from September 6 to 12. The first-of-its-kind exposure visit for Arunachal-based journalists was designed to familiarise the media with major projects and institutions shaping Gujarat’s development landscape. It also enabled the participating journalists to interact with officials, experts and stakeholders and gain a first-hand understanding of initiatives in infrastructure, urban planning, technology, industry, education, transportation, cooperative development and heritage conservation. Led by PIB Itanagar Joint Director Utsav Parmar, the delegation travelled across Ahmedabad, Dholera, Vadodara and Ekta Nagar, witnessing the State’s efforts to combine economic growth with technological advancement, institutional development and cultural preservation. Exploring Gandhian heritage and urban development The tour began in Ahmedabad with a visit to Kochrab Ashram, a site closely associated with Mahatma Gandhi’s early experiments in community living, self-reliance and public service. The visit offered the journalists an insight into the historical and philosophical foundations of the freedom movement and the continuing relevance of Gandhian values. The delegation also visited the Sabarmati Riverfront, an important urban development project that has transformed the riverfront into a public space incorporating recreation, civic amenities and environmental improvement, and boosting tourism. The visit provided an opportunity to observe how urban infrastructure can be planned alongside public access and city beautification. At CEPT University, Ahmedabad, the journalists were introduced to perspectives on architecture, urban planning, design and sustainable development. The interaction helped connect the broader themes of infrastructure creation and urban growth with the importance of planning, design and academic research. Dholera: A glimpse of the emerging industrial landscape One of the major highlights of the tour was the visit to the Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR), Gujarat, a greenfield development project envisioned as a major industrial and investment destination. The delegation explored the emerging infrastructure and industrial ecosystem of Dholera and gained an understanding of the planning and connectivity requirements involved in developing a modern industrial region. The visit offered insights into the role of integrated infrastructure, technology and investment facilitation in attracting industries and creating new economic opportunities. For the visiting journalists, Dholera presented a practical example of how large-scale development projects are conceived and implemented, and how emerging industrial centres can contribute to employment generation, investment and regional growth. The visit also included an external view of Tata’s semiconductor fabrication plant, described as India’s first large-scale semiconductor fabrication facility, which is currently under construction at Dholera. Technology, forensics and the changing world of work The visit to the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) provided the delegation with exposure to developments in forensic science, cyber security, investigation and emerging technologies. Follow Us On G -N e w s | Whatsapp Kashmir journalists on PIB tour reached Chennai on September 13, 2026 night The delegation, comprising 11 journalists and two PIB officials, arrived in Chennai on Sunday and was received by PIB Chennai officials at the Chennai International Airport.
